subject: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync

Team —

Quick ask as we prep the OrionHealth pilot: product needs a short-term soft commitment on Dedicated capacity during a canary period (detailed below) and we need procurement/infra alignment on timelines and fallback SLAs. High level:

- Pilot window: target Oct 20 — Nov 16 (4 weeks of canary + 1 week prep/teardown).
- Goal: sustained canary traffic for 2x expected production Q4 load for spike testing.
- Hardware mix concern: customer expects H100-class perf for model X; our current pools are A100/H100 mixed.

Asks:
1) Can infra provision a soft-reservation equivalent to ~10 H100 slots (or H100-equivalent capacity) that we can hold for the canary window as a reserved pool, with a defined fallback to burst lanes if not available?
2) What is the procurement timeline to add 10 H100 nodes (estimate needed by Oct 1 to meet Oct 20 start)?
3) Ops: we may need an autoscale policy exception for the canary (pre-warmed KV caches + prefix caching) to avoid cold-start noise in metrics. Can you outline what an "autoscale exemption" would require?
4) Product: we need a formal fallback SLA for degraded hardware (i.e., if only A100s are available) — acceptable latency deltas and model-variant fallbacks.

Attaching projected usage and a draft MOU for the pilot.

I don't expect all answers right away, but can you please reply with availability and any blockers by EOD tomorrow so we can surface to procurement?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Strategic Accounts (pilot programs)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: projected_usage_q4.csv, draft_mou_orion.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync

Thanks Rachel —

I can take the autoscale exemption work. A few clarifying items so we scope correctly:

- Baseline vs. stress: what's the expected baseline QPS/tokens for the canary and peak burst multiplier? Your CSV helps but a short summary here would speed things up.
- Canary window: is the Oct 20 start flexible by a week? Procurement lead times for H100 procurement are the gating factor.

Operational considerations for exemption:
- We can create a temporary reservation lane for the canary and mark it as "soft-commit" (non-preemptible for business hours). Outside those hours, it becomes preemptible.
- Exemption needs an ops-runbook page (I will draft) and a ticket in SUP-4217 for tracking.
- We will want a brief smoke test plan (p99 latency targets, token-throughput checks) and a rollback trigger (error rate + p99 degradation).

I'm attaching a template for autoscale-exempt requests so you can feed the product-level requirements into it (autoscale_exempt_template.docx).

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscale_exempt_template.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync

FWIW from product:

- The canary must demonstrate model X meeting the following: p99 <= 250ms (steady-state), throughput of 800k tokens/day during the canary stress periods, and consistent logits behavior vs. baseline.
- Fallback policy: if we cannot guarantee H100-equivalent latency, we want an automatic fallback to the quantized model variant that preserves quality targets with a documented latency tradeoff (we should specify an allowed p99 increase, e.g., +40%).
- Canary traffic: target 10% of customer traffic routed across the pilot for the first week, ramping to 35% by week 3.

I'll draft the performance acceptance criteria and drop it in the Drive folder (link below). For procurement, please bill this to OrionHealth cost center in the SOW and include a provisional budget line for temporary H100 rentals if full procurement can't land in time.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CanaryPlan_RK

Kimberly
Product Director — Inference Experience
Redwood Inference

(Added a short checklist to the Drive doc; will attach the acceptance criteria to the autoscale template.)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync

Short answer: yes, with caveats.

Capacity team notes:
- We can provision a temporary soft-commit equivalent to about 8 H100 slots (H100-equivalent based on perf-weighting) for a 4-week window, provided procurement signs off by Oct 1. If procurement is later, we can offer short-term rental capacity (cloud burst) but that adds ~30% to the cost estimate.
- Autoscale exemption: we'll need the exemption ticket created (SUP-4217) with the exact acceptance criteria, pre-warm strategy (KV cache + prefix cache warmers) and explicit eviction priority for the reservation lane. Without cache warmers, expect noisy p50/p95 during warmup.
- Hardware heterogeneity: if we must run on mixed A100/H100, we will require a model-variant fallback map and a quantization profile for the fallback variant to avoid quality regressions. Product needs to supply the variant names.

Attached a short capacity impact analysis. I can take procurement off your plate if you confirm the budget code and whether rentals are acceptable as contingency.

Marcus
Director, Resource Allocation
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_impact_analysis.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU pool fallback SLAs & procurement sync

Looping back — I will:

- Prepare a provisional SOW and budget estimate (attached: orion_sow_draft.pdf) that includes two options: full procurement (10 H100 nodes) and rental contingency (4-week rental to bridge start date).
- Coordinate with OrionHealth procurement (cc'd on the initial outreach) to confirm billing and MSA clauses. I'll push for an Oct 1 procurement decision but will flag the rental option as Plan B.
- Once we have the acceptance criteria from Kimberly and the autoscale-exempt ticket from Hannah, I'll update the SOW and send a version for internal sign-off.

Rachel — can you confirm Orion's willingness to accept rental contingency pricing if procurement cannot commit by Oct 1? If yes, I'll include a short clause in the SOW.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineering (pre-sales)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orion_sow_draft.pdf
